question: Which of the following performs the function of Credit Control in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Reserve Bank of India**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is responsible for credit control in India 
 
• Credit control is a tool used by the RBI to regulate the supply and demand of money in the economy.
 
• It's a key part of monetary policy
 
• The RBI controls credit by: 
 
 
• Regulating the credit extended by commercial banks to their customers 
 
• Ensuring the long-term development of the Indian economy 
 
• Helping the RBI and the government achieve economic growth 
 
• Keeping inflation under control 
 
• Purchasing and selling government securities in the open market 
 
• Using margin requirements, which is the difference between the current value of the security offered for loan and the value of loan granted 
 
 
 
• Credit control is a major tool for the RBI to achieve its goals

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• NITI Aayog
 
 
• NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) serves as the premier policy think tank of the Indian government.
 
• Established in 2015, it aims to foster cooperative federalism through the involvement of state governments in the policymaking process.
 
• One key function is to provide strategic and technical advice to the central and state governments, focusing on sustainable development and social equity. 
 
• Additionally, NITI Aayog has introduced initiatives like the Atal Innovation Mission to promote innovation and entrepreneurship in the country.
 
 
 
• Ministry of Finance
 
 
• The Ministry of Finance is responsible for managing the economic and financial affairs of the Indian government. It oversees various departments, including economic affairs, revenue, and expenditure.
 
• A crucial function of the ministry is formulating and implementing fiscal policies that drive economic growth, manage public debt, and ensure financial stability. 
 
• The ministry also prepares the annual Union Budget, outlining the government's expenditure and revenue for the coming fiscal year.
 
 
 
• Ministry of Education
 
 
• The Ministry of Education (formerly known as the Ministry of Human Resource Development) focuses on promoting and regulating education in India.
 
• It aims to ensure access to quality education at all levels, from primary to higher education.
 
• One significant initiative is the National Education Policy (NEP), which seeks to overhaul the educational framework by promoting holistic and multidisciplinary learning.
